q: Consider a Proclamation of Emergency: 1-Internal disturbance remains an available ground. 2-Armed rebellion is an available ground. 3-The Cabinet must recommend it in writing. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Internal disturbance was replaced by armed rebellion in 1978, when written Cabinet advice was also required.
why: The 1978 amendment changed the ground and added the writing requirement in the same exercise.
trapnote: One amendment made both changes. Learn the ground and the writing requirement together.

q: On approval of a Proclamation of Emergency, which statement is correct?
options: Both Houses must approve within two months by a special majority
Both Houses must approve within one month by a simple majority
Both Houses must approve within one month by a special majority
The House of the People alone must approve within one month
expl: One month, special majority, both Houses.
why: Each wrong option alters one variable only, so three separate facts must be held simultaneously.
trapnote: Three variables: which Houses, what period, what majority. Options change one at a time.

q: Consider the automatic suspension of the freedoms during an Emergency: 1-It operates on any ground of proclamation. 2-It is confined to the article containing the six freedoms. 3-It requires a separate Presidential order. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
None of them
expl: Only war/external triggers auto-freeze of that article; no order needed there, and only that article freezes.
why: Two of the three statements fail; only the confinement to the six freedoms is accurate.
trapnote: Automatic operation has an external trigger. A separate order belongs to the other provision.

q: Which statement about the protections against conviction and against deprivation of life is correct during an Emergency?
options: They may be suspended by a Presidential order specifying them
They cannot be suspended, the position having been settled by amendment in 1978
They may be suspended only where the ground is external aggression
They cannot be suspended, the position having been settled by amendment in 1971
expl: The 1978 amendment placed both beyond suspension.
why: The fourth option gives the right rule with the wrong year, which recognition alone will not catch.
trapnote: Right rule, wrong year is a standard construction. Verify both halves of an option.

q: On revocation of a Proclamation of Emergency by the House of the People, which statement is correct?
options: Notice by one-tenth of the members compels a special sitting, and a simple majority suffices
Notice by one-third of the members compels a special sitting, and a simple majority suffices
Notice by one-tenth of the members compels a special sitting, and a special majority is needed
A resolution of both Houses by special majority is required for revocation
expl: One-tenth for the notice, simple majority to disapprove.
why: The asymmetry is the point: approval needs a special majority while disapproval needs only a simple one.
trapnote: Approval and disapproval require different majorities. That asymmetry is deliberate and tested.

q: Consider President's Rule in a State: 1-It may be proclaimed on the Governor's report or otherwise. 2-Both Houses must approve within two months. 3-A special majority is required for approval. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The report is not indispensable and approval is by simple majority within two months.
why: The majority requirement is the planted defect; candidates import it from the national provision.
trapnote: The two emergencies differ on period and on majority. Do not carry one rule into the other.

q: On continuance of President's Rule beyond one year, which statement is correct?
options: A resolution of both Houses by special majority is sufficient for the extension
The Election Commission must certify, no other condition being required
A Proclamation of Emergency must be in force, no other condition being required
A Proclamation of Emergency must be in force and the Election Commission must certify
expl: Both conditions operate cumulatively beyond the first year.
why: Two options give one of the two conditions, so partial knowledge produces a near miss rather than a clear error.
trapnote: Two cumulative conditions. An option offering only one of them is incomplete and therefore wrong.

q: Consider the 1994 decision on President's Rule: 1-A proclamation is justiciable. 2-Majority is to be tested on the floor of the House. 3-A dismissed government cannot be restored. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The Court may restore a dismissed government where the proclamation fails.
why: Restoration is the limb most often omitted, because it is the most striking remedy the decision recognised.
trapnote: Four holdings in that case. Restoration and secularism are the two most often dropped.

q: The financial emergency provision has been invoked:
options: On no occasion since the Constitution commenced
On one occasion, during the crisis of 1991
On two occasions, in 1966 and in 1991
On one occasion, during the crisis of 1966
expl: It has never been proclaimed.
why: Two options attach it to genuine economic crises, which is what makes them credible.
trapnote: Never invoked. The crises named in the distractors are real, which is why they persuade.

q: Consider the effect of a financial emergency: 1-Salaries of State public servants may be reduced. 2-Salaries of judges of the higher judiciary may be reduced. 3-Money Bills of a State may be reserved for the President. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three consequences are expressly provided for.
why: The second is the one candidates doubt, judicial salaries otherwise being protected from variation.
trapnote: Judicial salaries, normally protected, are expressly reachable during a financial emergency.

q: Which statement distinguishes the automatic suspension provision from the provision suspending the remedy?
options: The first needs an order and reaches all rights; the second is automatic and confined to one article
Both are automatic; the first covers all rights and the second covers one article only
Both need an order; the first excludes two articles and the second covers one article only
The first is automatic and covers one article; the second needs an order, never two articles
expl: Trigger, instrument, scope and carve-out all differ between the two provisions.
why: Each wrong option swaps exactly one attribute, so four variables must be held at once.
trapnote: Four variables separate these two provisions. Check each rather than relying on a summary phrase.

q: A Proclamation of Emergency is in force. Consider: 1-The term of the House of the People may be extended by one year at a time. 2-Such extension may continue for six months after the Proclamation ceases. 3-The extension requires ratification by the States. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Extension is by law of Parliament and needs no State ratification.
why: The third statement imports the federal ratification requirement, which has no application here.
trapnote: Ratification attaches to specified federal amendments only. It does not attach to term extension.

q: On martial law, which statement is correct?
options: Parliament may indemnify acts done in connection with its maintenance
A State legislature may indemnify such acts within its own territory
Indemnity follows automatically once martial law is withdrawn
Martial law is a separate category of Emergency requiring proclamation
expl: Indemnity requires a law of Parliament; martial law is not one of the three Emergencies.
why: The fourth option is attractive because martial law is discussed alongside the Emergency provisions.
trapnote: Martial law is not one of the three Emergencies and appears in a different provision altogether.

q: Parliament restricts the rights of members of the armed forces to ensure discipline. Which statement is correct?
options: The restriction is valid only during a Proclamation of Emergency
The restriction is valid if made by either Parliament or a State legislature
The restriction is valid, the power being vested in Parliament alone
The restriction is invalid, fundamental rights being available to all citizens
expl: The power is exclusive to Parliament and does not depend on an Emergency.
why: The third option is the institution-swap trap and is the most plausible of the three wrong answers.
trapnote: This power belongs to Parliament exclusively and operates in ordinary times.

q: Consider the three Emergencies: 1-The national Emergency has been proclaimed three times. 2-President's Rule has been used on over a hundred occasions. 3-The financial emergency has been used once. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The financial emergency has never been used; the other two counts are accurate.
why: Two accurate figures are paired with one false one, so the candidate must check each independently.
trapnote: Three counts, one false. Verify each rather than accepting the set on the strength of two.

q: Andhra Pradesh was placed under President's Rule in January 1973. Which statement correctly identifies the context?
options: The Telangana agitation of 1969, which led to the Gentlemen's Agreement of that year
The Jai Andhra agitation, which led to the Six-Point Formula and a constitutional amendment
The reorganisation of the State under the States Reorganisation Act of 1956
The bifurcation of the State under the Reorganisation Act of 2014
expl: The 1972-73 agitation produced President's Rule, the Six-Point Formula and the 1973 amendment.
why: The second option names a real agitation and attaches it to an agreement of the wrong decade.
trapnote: The Gentlemen's Agreement belongs to 1956, before the merger, not to the 1969 agitation.

q: A Proclamation is issued on the ground of armed rebellion and an officer treats all freedoms as suspended. Which statement is correct?
options: No freedom is automatically suspended on that ground, and two articles can never be suspended
All freedoms are automatically suspended, two articles alone remaining enforceable
The six freedoms alone are automatically suspended, other rights requiring an order
No freedom is automatically suspended, though any right may be suspended by order
expl: Automatic suspension requires an external ground, and two articles are beyond suspension entirely.
why: The fourth option gets the first limb right and the second wrong, which is the near-miss construction.
trapnote: Two independent limbs. An option correct on one and wrong on the other is still wrong.

q: Consider the recommendations on the use of President's Rule: 1-One commission recommended it be a last resort. 2-A later commission endorsed that approach. 3-Those recommendations are binding on the Union. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Commission recommendations are advisory; the binding discipline came from the 1994 decision.
why: The third statement confuses persuasive recommendations with the judicial holding that gave them effect.
trapnote: Commissions advise; courts bind. The 1994 decision converted the advice into enforceable discipline.

q: During a Proclamation of Emergency, the Union may give directions to a State. Which statement is correct?
options: The Union may legislate on State subjects only with the State's prior consent
The Union's power to direct arises only where President's Rule has been proclaimed
The Union may dissolve the State legislature without any further proclamation
The Union may direct a State as to the manner of exercise of its executive power
expl: Directions as to the exercise of State executive power are expressly permitted.
why: The third option conflates the two provisions, which is the most common structural confusion in the topic.
trapnote: The national Emergency and President's Rule have different effects on the State machinery.

q: Consider: 1-Secularism was held to be part of the basic structure in 1994. 2-That holding arose in a case on President's Rule. 3-The same case held the proclamation to be a non-justiciable political question. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The case held the proclamation justiciable, which is the opposite of the third statement.
why: The third statement states the position that prevailed before that very decision, which is why it reads plausibly.
trapnote: A superseded position offered as the holding of the case that superseded it is a favourite construction.
